newsitem.title: UK: UK ready to cancel 16 mln stg Zimbabwe aid debt.
newsitem.headline: UK ready to cancel 16 mln stg Zimbabwe aid debt.

text.p: Britain's Overseas Development Agency said on Wednesday it was prepared to cancel 16 million pounds ($26.14 million) of Zimbabwe's aid debt if Harare reached a new deal with the International Monetary Fund.
A spokeswoman for the ODA said debt forgiveness was dependent on an accord being reached with the IMF, which she added was likely to take some time.

Zimbabwe Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said in December the government would continue to try to reduce its spending and budget deficit, both essential for it to secure IMF and other Western donor aid for a new programme of economic reforms it plans to launch this year.
The IMF and the World Bank said they were unlikely to provide financial suport to the new five-year reform programme until the government showed progress in cutting state spending.
They withheld some aid to Zimbabwe in 1995 after the government failed to meet some cost-saving targets.

The ODA's comments followed a report in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Tuesday which said Britain was considering cancelling Harare's short-term debt of about Z$288 million (US$25.4 million).

The story quoted Murerwa as saying that during talks in London last week with Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, the British government had pledged to support Zimbabwe's privatisation and indigenisation process.
It also said Britain would consider cancelling Zimbabwe's short-term debt if the country came up with a second plan of action for economic reform.
However the ODA said the debt it was prepared to cancel concerned development loans and aid debt, not short-term debt.

The second phase of reforms, titled the Zimbabwe Programme for Economic and Social Transformation, should be launched this year once the consultation process in government and with industry and labour has been completed.
